metadata.description: AST-expansion conformance fixture for grids/sectional_volume_1d/rules/growth_lr2m_D_bin_closed: a minimal consuming model binding NCELL=2, NBIN=4, NTRACER=1 at the import edges, writing dN/dt = -D(lam*N, V, wrt: bin) with the section number N, the section volume V and the relative growth rate lam all declared [cell, bin]. The two-operand compound match must fire through the fixpoint (priority 10, where lam, N, V: [cell, bin]) and lower to the rule's three-region makearray -- interior sections [2, 3] holding the imported sectional_lr2m_growth_number_interior stencil, section 1 and section 4 holding the closed-end regions that drop the outer edge flux (section 1: up-flux through its upper edge minus the down-flux of section 2; section 4: down-flux through its lower edge minus the up-flux of section 3). The model follows the grid's consumer-supplied-geometry contract: the 5-edge array vb comes from the grid's shared test grid mesh/mms_sections.esm (vb[kn] = 2^((kn-1)/4)), read by the rule's stencils by bare name. The golden pins the byte-identical post-lowering AST, in the esm-spec 9.6.4 reference-preserving form (stencil and mesh template references survive uninlined in the document's template registry), across bindings.
metadata.name: growth_lr2m_D_bin_closed_ast_fixture

mms_sections_vb.description: Section edge volumes of the geometric test grid: vb[kn] = 2^((kn - 1)/NBIN) over kn in bin_nodes.

sectional_total.description: Per-cell total sum_j N[c,j] over the size sections of a [cell, bin] section moment (number, or volume), shape [cell]: the quantity every flux-form operator on this grid conserves exactly, since each lowers to edge fluxes that cancel in pairs between neighbouring sections and vanish at the two closed ends of the size range. Aggregation index `gj`, so it never captures a consuming rule's own index when inlined.

V.description: Section volume moment, 1.5 times the number (mean volume 1.5 um^3 in every section).

vb.description: Section edge volumes, mms_sections_vb at NBIN=4.
